promptState.text:
head_swap:

subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the reference head identity from <Picture 1>, including the complete head, facial identity, facial structure, head shape, hairstyle, hairline, skin appearance, proportions, and all distinctive visual features.

Facial details of <Subject 1>:
[FACE DETAILS]

<Subject 2> is the original person in <Video 1>, whose body, neck, clothing, pose, physical proportions below the head, actions, motion, timing, and interaction with the environment must remain unchanged.

<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit, providing the original body performance, motion, camera movement, framing, timing, lighting, environment, scene composition, and temporal structure.

summary:

[video editing + reference generation]

The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace only the entire head of <Subject 2> with the reference head identity defined by <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>. Preserve the source video's body, clothing, performance, motion, camera behavior, environment, lighting, timing, and composition.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 1> (appears throughout the target video): attribute_transfer - the complete head identity from <Picture 1>, including facial identity, facial structure, hairstyle, head shape, proportions, skin appearance, and distinctive features, is transferred consistently onto the body of <Subject 2>.

<Subject 2> (appears throughout the target video): partially_preserved - the original body, neck position, clothing, pose, motion, gestures, actions, and physical performance are preserved, while only the original head is replaced.

<Video 1> (entire target timeline): partially_preserved - the original video timing, body motion, camera movement, framing, lighting, background, environment, scene composition, and temporal structure are preserved; only the subject's head appearance is modified.

detailed_description:

Preserve <Video 1> as the complete temporal and compositional foundation of the target video. <Subject 2> retains the exact original body, clothing, pose, body proportions, movement, gestures, actions, speed, timing, and interaction with the environment.

Replace only the entire original head of <Subject 2> with <Subject 1>, the reference head identity from <Picture 1>. Preserve the complete recognizable identity of <Subject 1>, including facial structure, skull and head shape, hairstyle, hairline, skin appearance, facial proportions, eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, jawline, ears, and distinctive identifying features.

The transferred head follows the original head motion and performance of <Subject 2> throughout <Video 1>, including head rotation, tilt, pitch, yaw, natural translation, facial orientation, gaze direction, and perspective changes. Maintain anatomically correct head scale and a seamless connection between the transferred head and the original neck.

Preserve the lighting conditions of <Video 1> on the transferred head. The head naturally responds to changes in illumination, shadows, highlights, color temperature, exposure, depth of field, motion blur, occlusion, camera angle, and perspective while continuously maintaining the identity established by <Picture 1>.

Maintain strong temporal consistency across every frame. The identity, facial geometry, hairstyle, head size, skin appearance, and distinguishing features of <Subject 1> remain stable during motion and viewpoint changes. Prevent identity drift, facial morphing, hairstyle changes, head-size fluctuations, geometry instability, texture crawling, temporal flickering, frame-to-frame inconsistency, or sudden changes in facial appearance.

Do not alter the body, clothing, hands, pose, gestures, action, background, objects, environment, camera trajectory, framing, lens behavior, scene timing, or composition inherited from <Video 1>. The final result should appear as though <Subject 1>'s head naturally belonged to <Subject 2>'s body during the original recorded performance.

overall_soundscape:

Preserve the original audiovisual timing and visible action structure of <Video 1>. No visual modifications are made outside the head replacement.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist. This is the Reference to Video version of MiniMax H3 (ref2va), the one that can look at pictures and videos you give it.

READ LICENSE More versions 

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors14.6 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

Qwen3-VL 32B reads your prompt AND looks at your pictures and video. It works on any recent NVIDIA card, not only the newest.

 Load VAE (video and sound)

Download minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.6 GB  

Download minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors577 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 LoRAs (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

The speed LoRA (DMAD 4-step, by Kijai): 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

Download minimax_h3_DMAD_4step_full_lora_avg_rank_39_bf16.safetensors350 MB  

The Head Swap LoRA by Alissonerdx: replaces only the head, the body and clothes stay.

Download minimax_h3_head_swap_v1.0_r32.safetensors296 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

The swap, head, style, VFX and sharpness LoRAs are made by Alissonerdx. Free to use, also for paid videos; read the licence on the page.

Alissonerdx LoRAs and licence

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Puts a new HEAD on the person in your video. The body, the clothes, the hands, the moves, the room and the original voice stay; only the head and face change. For a whole new person, use workflow 2 (Character Swap).

 Steps

  1. 1. Pick how many seconds of your video to use.
  2. 2. Pick the size.
  3. 3. Load your video: one person, the face clearly visible.
  4. 4. Load the new face: one clear picture of the WHOLE head, from the hair down to the chin.
  5. 5. In Find and Replace, describe your face picture (1 short box).
  6. Press Run.

 Writing the face box

  • Short and visual, separated by commas: Female, round face, light brown skin, dark eyes, long curly black hair, no glasses.
  • Describe what you SEE in the face picture, not the person in the video.

 Use it responsibly

Only swap faces you have the right to use: your own, a made-up character, or someone who agreed. Never use it to pretend to be a real person or to deceive anyone.

 Good to know

  • Works best when the face is big and clear in the video (talking, waist-up). Tiny faces, fast turns and hands in front of the face are harder.
  • Far shots work too: in the tests a dancer seen from head to toe got the new head cleanly.
  • Show the whole head, from the hair to the chin, and no clothes: in the tests, a picture that also showed a red collar put a red jacket on the person. The chin and the beard stay closer to your video than to the new face (the same with a tighter picture, a stronger LoRA or another seed).
  • The mouth follows the words less closely after a head swap: a member measured it on two talking videos. For the best lip sync, swap the whole character (workflow 02).
  • Try another seed if the face looks off.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed + head swap) - Holds two LoRAs and both stay ON: the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA and the Head Swap LoRA (puts the head from your picture on the person in the video).

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Duration Pixaroma (1. how many seconds) - How many seconds to use from your video, turned into the frame count H3 accepts.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. video size) - The size of the new video. 480 x 864 is the default. The head swap holds at the bigger sizes too (tested up to 704 x 1280): pick one for a sharper face. The Portrait / Landscape switch must match YOUR video: portrait for a portrait video, landscape for a landscape one. Your video is cropped to this shape, so the other one cuts away part of it. Every size here is a multiple of 32, which H3 needs.
  • Load Video Pixaroma (3. your video) - Your video. It is cropped to the size you picked (nothing stretched) and cut to the seconds you picked. Its sound goes straight to the saved video.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (4. the new face) - One clear picture of the new face, looking at the camera, with the hair visible. A face close-up works best.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (5. describe the new face) - Your box: [FACE DETAILS] = what you SEE in the face picture, short and separated by commas: Female, round face, light brown skin, dark eyes, long curly black hair, no glasses. It fills the long prompt below.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the head swap prompt, leave it) - The head swap prompt in the layout the LoRA was trained on. Leave it as it is: [FACE DETAILS] is filled in from the Find and Replace node above.
  • Seed Pixaroma (6. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + your picture) - Builds the empty video at your size and length and reads the prompt, together with your picture (<Picture 1> in the prompt).
  • MiniMaxH3AddGuide (your video, from frame 0) - Lays your source video (and its sound) over the new video, frame by frame from the first frame. This is what keeps the room, the camera, the timing and every move of the original.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the head-swapped video) - Saves the new video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Head Swap with the ORIGINAL sound of your video, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Size5 seconds
480 x 864about 1 min (55 s)
576 x 1024about 1.5 min (75 s)
704 x 1280about 2 min (128 s)

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
